# Tractor Supply Co (TSCO) Deep Dive Analysis

Report 011 | Published 2020-03-01 | Evaluated 2026-11-07

[Original member article](https://www.lynalden.com/premium-2020-3-1/) | [Article index](README.md) | [Structured review](../data/reviews/011.json)

Crisis positioning, gold exposure and rural-retail value.

The near-term risk and policy-response calls were useful. Tractor Supply's business performed better than a generic recession template suggested, while Petsense provided negative acquisition evidence. The Swiss-safety framing needs legal/custody distinctions. Long-horizon value targets remain pending or data-limited.

**Coverage:** All numbered text blocks and image labels read. Material theses, forecasts and explanations are included; routine holdings lists, incidental statistics, company descriptions and boilerplate are excluded. Chart pixels were not inspected.

**Direction:** See reason; no return inferred.

**Timing:** No fixed endpoint supplied.

**Mechanism:** Outcome evidence does not independently identify causation.

**Reviewer confidence:** medium

**Outcome evidence:**

- [Fiscal 2020 results](https://ir.tractorsupply.com/newsroom/news-releases/news-releases-details/2021/Tractor-Supply-Company-Reports-Fourth-Quarter-and-Fiscal-2020-Results-and-Increases-Quarterly-Dividend-By-30/default.aspx) | Tractor Supply | 2021-01-28 | Verified in the audit

2020 sales increased 27.2%, comparable sales 23.1%, and net income rose to $749 million. Petsense incurred $74.1 million impairment. Q4 gross margin increased 75 basis points; dividend was raised 30% in January 2021.
